claims.text: Standard laser powder bed fusion produces AlCrFeNiSi components with significant residual stresses caused by rapid solidification and high thermal gradients.
Standard laser powder bed fusion produces microstructural heterogeneity in AlCrFeNiSi components.
Conventional high-thermal-load additive manufacturing degrades the mechanical properties of AlCrFeNiSi, including by causing brittleness.
Conventional processing of AlCrFeNiSi entails processing complexity related to rapid solidification.
An HPHT treatment at approximately 6 GPa and 1473 K for 2 hours is an applicable post-processing window for miniature AlCrFeNiSi components.
Rapid quenching after HPHT is an applicable part of the treatment for AlCrFeNiSi components.
The proposed HPHT treatment is applicable to additively manufactured AlCrFeNiSi components with millimeter-scale dimensions.
HPHT treatment will induce a hierarchically patterned microstructure in AlCrFeNiSi.
HPHT treatment will refine the grains of AlCrFeNiSi.
HPHT treatment will form coherent interphase boundaries in AlCrFeNiSi.
The HPHT-induced microstructure will homogenize the phase distribution in AlCrFeNiSi.
High pressure and temperature enhance atomic diffusion, which promotes stress relaxation and grain refinement.
HPHT treatment will smooth compositional gradients in AlCrFeNiSi.
Coherent interfaces and compositional homogenization will eliminate residual thermal stresses in AlCrFeNiSi.
HPHT-treated AlCrFeNiSi components will have lower residual stresses than untreated components made under conventional high-thermal-load AM conditions.
HPHT-treated AlCrFeNiSi components will exhibit higher tensile strength and ductility than conventionally manufactured or untreated components.
Adding HPHT post-processing will reduce overall processing complexity relative to conventional high-thermal-load additive-manufacturing methods.
Departures from the controlled HPHT window could produce unwanted phase changes or loss of silicon-related phases in AlCrFeNiSi.
HPHT treatment has enhanced both strength and ductility in another high-entropy alloy system.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis claims reduced processing complexity, but the intervention retains standard laser powder bed fusion and adds a dedicated 6 GPa, 1473 K post-processing step in specialized equipment. No field explains how this additional operation reduces total complexity.
